source.title: Transfer Entropy and O-Information to Detect Grokking in Tensor Network Multi-Class Classification Problems
source.authors: Domenico Pomarico; Roberto Cilli; A. Monaco; L. Bellantuono; M. La Rocca; T. Maggipinto; Giuseppe Magnifico; Marlis Ontivero Ortega; E. Pantaleo; S. Tangaro; S. Stramaglia; R. Bellotti; N. Amoroso

record.file_problem: Full text is present; it contains minor character-encoding artifacts, but is readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests grokking-like behavior in MPS classifiers on image and hyperspectral datasets, extending the investigation to non-algorithmic classification settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports accuracy dynamics and O-information dynamics relevant to V2 and V3. It also reports entanglement, magnetization, and transfer-entropy results, but these do not directly measure the circuit formation or removal of memorizing components named in V2, nor a separate test-accuracy outcome.
record.test_reason: The study trains MPS tensor-network classifiers on non-algorithmic data (Fashion MNIST, PRISMA hyperspectral imagery) and reports whether a grokking-like transition occurs. That bears on V3's claim of grokking-like delays on non-algorithmic data. Its O-information tracking bears weakly on V2's progress-measure part.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude Fashion MNIST shows a grokking transition marked by redundancy (positive O-information), entanglement compression and directional mask information flow, while the hyperspectral model stays synergistic and overfit without grokking.
record.recipe_differences: Uses two-site gradient descent to train MPS classifiers with a mean squared error objective on three-class Fashion MNIST and PRISMA land-cover data. It does not use small algorithmic datasets or modular arithmetic; it measures accuracy and information-theoretic quantities rather than reproducing the original algorithmic grokking setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes differ between the Fashion MNIST and PRISMA tasks and among Fashion MNIST classes. No initialization-scale or weight-norm sweep is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Entanglement entropy drops from volume-law to sub-volume-law, and label-specific magnetization structure appears around the transition (sweep ~10 for Fashion MNIST, ~50 for PRISMA). This happens in both grokking and non-grokking tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking in tensor-network classifiers coincides with an entanglement-entropy transition.

fits_no_version.finding: Transfer entropy between class masks is asymmetric in Fashion MNIST (TE1→0 z≈1.5, up to 2.78 for strongly magnetized spins) and flat for PRISMA.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Directional information flow between class-specific components accompanies grokking-like generalization.

record.problems: The text does not give exact overall test-accuracy values or the precise timing of test improvement relative to training-accuracy saturation. Accuracy uncertainty is not stated in the text. Fashion MNIST performance is highly uneven across classes, and no initialization-scale or weight-norm intervention is tested.
record.rows_left_out: Entanglement-entropy, magnetization, and transfer-entropy descriptions are not included as rows because they do not directly measure the circuit identity/removal mechanism in V2 or the test-accuracy behavior in V3. Their results are described in Sections III.B–C and Figures 4–6.

untested.parts: Switching the delay on or off via initialization scale or weight norm (lazy-to-rich); text and molecule data.
Identification of a generalizing circuit (e.g. Fourier) and later removal of memorizing components.
Small algorithmic datasets; dependence of delay on training-set size.

missing.what: Relative timing of the training-accuracy plateau and the test-accuracy rise in Fashion MNIST, needed to confirm any delay.

record.verdict_notes: Single runs are reported, with no seeds or uncertainty on accuracies. The 'grokking' label rests largely on the authors' interpretation: overall training accuracy is ~70%, and no delay between fitting and generalization is quantified in the text. MPS models trained by two-site gradient descent with an MSE loss are far from the original transformer setup.

versions.untested_parts: Small algorithmic datasets, chance-to-near-perfect test accuracy after training accuracy saturation, and the effect of training-set size are not tested.

The study measures O-information as a progress indicator, but does not identify a Fourier or other generalizing circuit, show memorizing components being removed, or test these mechanisms on small algorithmic datasets.
Tests image and hyperspectral data, but does not vary initialization scale or weight norm, and does not test text or molecule datasets.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning is studied.
No weight-decay or low-norm intervention, efficiency comparison, critical dataset size, or ungrokking test is reported.
The study does not compare algorithms learned across runs or vary architecture and hyperparameters to test convergence to the same algorithm.
No adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point/softmax artifact controls are tested.

rows.value: The paper describes a grokking transition with a sharp improvement in test accuracy, while also stating that overall test accuracy is limited by poor generalization on the bag class.
rows.note: The text does not give an overall test-accuracy value or the exact timing of the improvement relative to training-accuracy saturation.
rows.check: The authors assert a grokking transition with sharp test improvement. The text gives no overall test value and no evidence the rise lags training saturation; the transition at sweep ~8-10 coincides with training-side changes.

rows.subject: MPS classifier on fashion MNIST (dress, sneaker, bag)
rows.operation_detail: Tracked O-information among the three output scores during training.
rows.value: Jumps into the positive regime around sweep 8–9, peaks, and then stabilizes; the text also describes a moderate peak forecasting the transition jump during the preceding MPS sweep.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviation across the six variable-order permutations is shown; no numerical uncertainty is stated in the text.
rows.note: The authors interpret the positive regime as redundancy and associate the transition with grokking. The precise O-information values are shown in the figure, not stated in the text.
rows.check: O-information jumps abruptly, coinciding with the transition, rather than rising gradually beforehand. Only a 'moderate peak' one sweep earlier forecasts it. The measure is an output-score statistic, not a circuit or memorization measure.

source_check.correct: State: cannot_determine for V2. Output-score O-information becomes positive around sweeps 8–9, with a moderate peak one sweep earlier; gradual formation of a generalizing circuit and subsequent removal of memorizing components are not measured.

rows.subject: MPS classifier on hyperspectral land-cover data
rows.operation_detail: Tracked O-information among the three output scores during training.
rows.value: Changes more gradually around sweep 46 but remains negative after the transition; the text also describes a moderate peak forecasting the transition jump during the preceding MPS sweep.

rows.check: No grokking occurs on this task, so the row cannot show a progress measure anticipating grokking. A similar pre-transition peak is reported here too, which suggests the forecast signal is not specific to grokking.

relationships.reason: Authors call it grokking, but training saturates at only ~70%, bag never fits, and the text shows no lag of test behind training accuracy (r1, r2, r5, r6).
relationships.display_finding: Training accuracy saturated near 70%, the bag class remained unfitted, and test accuracy showed no lag behind training despite the authors' grokking description.
